profile.name: Megan Schutt
profile.writeup:
Some bowlers rely on pace, others on movement, but Megan Schutt has built her reputation on making the ball talk. One of Australia's most dependable fast bowlers of the modern era, Schutt has been a constant presence in the national setup for well over a decade. Known for her ability to swing the new ball, particularly with her trademark inswinger, she has troubled batters across formats and delivered on some of the biggest stages. From being a leading wicket-taker at the 2013 Women's World Cup to playing a central role in Australia's dominant run in global tournaments, her career has been defined by consistency and an ability to rise to the occasion.


Born in Adelaide, South Australia, in January 1993, Schutt began making her mark in domestic cricket at a young age. She made her debut for the South Australian Scorpions in the Women's National Cricket League during the 2009-10 season, aged just 16. Her performances soon brought her into the Australia A setup, where she impressed enough to earn a national call-up. She made her ODI debut against New Zealand in December 2012, followed by her T20I debut against the same opposition in January 2013. Her international arrival could hardly have been more impressive. Selected for the 2013 Women's World Cup in India, she finished as the tournament's leading wicket-taker with 15 scalps in 7 matches. She also claimed two important wickets in the final against West Indies as Australia lifted the trophy.


Schutt continued to establish herself as a regular in the Australian attack, playing an important role in the team's successful 2015 Ashes campaign in England. Her career, however, reached another level in 2018. During a T20I against India, she became the first Australian woman to take a hat-trick in the format. She followed it up with another hat-trick in an ODI against the West Indies in 2019, becoming the first woman to claim two international hat-tricks. Her ability to strike early and make life difficult for opposition batters made her an important part of Australia's white-ball plans, with her variations and accuracy adding another dimension to the attack.


The 2020 T20 World Cup in Australia provided one of the defining chapters of her career. Schutt finished as the tournament's leading wicket-taker with 13 scalps, including a match-winning spell of 4/18 in the final against India at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. In front of a record crowd, she dismissed Shafali Verma early in the chase, setting the tone for Australia's title-winning performance. She remained a key contributor as Australia went on to win the 2022 ODI World Cup in New Zealand and the 2023 T20 World Cup in South Africa. By then, she had firmly established herself among the leading fast bowlers in the women's game.


Her individual milestones continued to pile up. Schutt became the first woman to reach 150 T20I wickets in 2025, underlining her longevity and consistency in the shortest format. In September that year, she also brought up her 300th international wicket, joining Ellyse Perry as only the second Australian woman to reach the landmark. In October 2026, she became just the third Australian woman to claim 150 ODI wickets. Her contribution has extended into domestic cricket as well, where she has been a regular for Adelaide Strikers in the Women's Big Bash League, playing a major role in their title-winning campaign in 2022-23.
